authors: Monoarfa, T.A.; Sumarwan, U.; Suroso, A.I.; Wulandari, R.
title: Switch or Stay? Applying a Push-Pull-Mooring Framework to Evaluate Behavior in E-Grocery Shopping
source_location: Open-access MDPI full text: Section 3.1-3.2 (sampling, instrument), Table 2 (alphas), Table 3 (direct paths), Table 4 (moderation), Appendix A Table A1 (items)
hypothesis_supported: H1 (dissatisfaction n.s.), H2 (attractiveness significant), H5 (switching cost POSITIVE sign; contrary to hypothesised direction)
context: Jakarta, Indonesia; switching from physical markets TO e-grocery apps (channel adoption, not platform-to-platform)
method: CB-SEM (AMOS); 39 items, 5 removed after modification indices
constructs: Dissatisfaction (push), alternative attractiveness (pull), switching cost (mooring), plus ease of use, usefulness, value, health consciousness, innovativeness
measurement: 5-point Likert; switching-cost items concern the effort/learning of changing TO e-grocery (e.g. 'It would take a lot of time changing to e-grocery shopping'); alphas: DSAT .936, ATT .939, SWC .929, SWI .901
key_findings: Table 3: dissatisfaction -> switching intention 0.127 (p=.069, not supported); attractiveness -> switching intention 0.314 (p=.015); switching cost -> switching intention 0.294 (p=.017, positive). Table 4: switching-cost x dissatisfaction/attractiveness interactions negative
relevance: Verified precedent for a positive switching-cost coefficient when items describe the effort of changing to the alternative (similar wording to SC1 in the present survey); context differs from platform-to-platform switching
